related_questions.question: How do you tell if your lungs are inflamed?

text_blocks.snippet: Lung inflammation, also known as pneumonitis, can manifest through various symptoms, including shortness of breath, chest pain, and a dry cough. Other potential indicators include fever, wheezing, and coughing up mucus or blood. If you experience these symptoms, especially if they are persistent or severe, it's crucial to consult a doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: shortness of breath, chest pain, and a dry cough

text_blocks.snippet: Several conditions can cause lung inflammation, including:

list.title: Pneumonia:
list.snippet: An infection that causes inflammation and fluid buildup in the lungs, leading to symptoms like cough with mucus, fever, and difficulty breathing.

list.title: Bronchitis:
list.snippet: Inflammation of the airways (bronchi) that can cause a persistent cough, often with mucus.

list.title: Pleurisy:
list.snippet: Inflammation of the lining of the lungs (pleura) that can cause sharp chest pain that worsens with breathing or coughing.

list.title: Asthma:
list.snippet: A chronic respiratory disease that can cause inflammation and narrowing of the airways, leading to wheezing and shortness of breath.

list.title: Pulmonary Edema:
list.snippet: A condition where excess fluid builds up in the lungs, causing shortness of breath, coughing up blood, and a feeling of suffocation.

list.title: Pulmonary Fibrosis:
list.snippet: A condition where lung tissue becomes scarred and thickened, leading to shortness of breath and a dry cough.

text_blocks.snippet: If you experience any of the following symptoms, it's crucial to seek medical attention:

list.snippet: Persistent cough, especially with mucus or blood
Chest pain that worsens with breathing or coughing

text_blocks.snippet: A doctor may use various methods to diagnose lung inflammation, including:

list.snippet: Physical exam: Listening to your lungs with a stethoscope and assessing your symptoms.
Chest X-ray or CT scan: Imaging tests to visualize the lungs and identify any abnormalities.
Blood tests: To check for signs of infection or inflammation.
Lung function tests: To assess how well your lungs are working.
Bronchoscopy: A procedure to examine the airways with a camera.
Biopsy: A procedure to collect a tissue sample for examination.

related_questions.question: Can having COVID damage your lungs?
related_questions.snippet: COVID-19 infections can cause lung damage that leads to pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) or scarring.
